questions.explanation: Concept discrimination: Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis (SPPS) is uniquely defined by: 'An automated peptide synthesis method where peptide chains are assembled stepwise while covalently anchored to an insoluble polymer resin bead.'. The alternative statements erroneously attribute principles of 'Protecting Group Orthogonality', 'Protein Secondary Structure', or 'Disulfide Bridge' to 'Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis (SPPS)'.

questions.question: Which statement best discriminates 'Protecting Group Orthogonality' from other related principles in Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins?

options.label: A
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Protecting Group Orthogonality is properly defined as: The specific pH at which an amino acid or protein possesses no net electrical charge and does not migrate in an electric field.

options.label: B
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Protecting Group Orthogonality is properly defined as: The dipolar, electrically neutral ionic form of an amino acid containing both a protonated ammonium group (-NH₃⁺) and a deprotonated carboxylate group (-COO⁻).

options.label: C
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Protecting Group Orthogonality is properly defined as: A carboxylic acid containing an amino group (-NH₂) bonded directly to the α-carbon atom adjacent to the carboxyl group.

options.label: D
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, Protecting Group Orthogonality specifically denotes: A synthetic strategy utilizing protecting groups (such as Fmoc and Boc) that can be removed independently without affecting other protected sites.
